Central — Liverpool, United Kingdom

🟢 Official crime data · Merseyside Police, data.police.uk Methodology →

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Merseyside Police recorded 3,033 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 40.7 per 1,000 residents, the 1st highest rate of Liverpool's 30 wards. The daytime score here is driven by drugs (150), shoplifting (149), burglary (26); the evening/night score by violent crime (271), anti social behaviour (132), public order (82). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

This rating is derived from Merseyside Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic covering this area, not an assessment of it. It is a periodic snapshot rather than a live feed, and it is normalised against residents rather than footfall; the methodology page sets out the year, the normalisation and what that means for busy central areas.

Frequently asked questions

Is Central safe?

Wandroz currently rates Central in Liverpool as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Liverpool during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Liverpool at night. This rating is derived from Merseyside Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Central safe at night?

At night, Central is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Liverpool. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Central a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Central's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Liverpool) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

Is there official crime data for Central?

Yes. Central's rating is derived from Merseyside Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk, not an assessment — see the note on this page for the exact figure and the methodology page for full sourcing.
